label: June Park, sysop
blurb: One phone line, 300 baud, and every caller greeted by name.

person.name: June Park
person.relation: mother, ran a bulletin board called The Marigold from the spare room

cards.text: She ran a bulletin board called The Marigold off one phone line in the spare room, and the computer had to be off the hook to answer it.
The modem ran at 300 baud, so a single paragraph of ASCII art took four minutes to draw on your screen.
She wrote the welcome screen herself, one character at a time, and it ended with a rose made of punctuation marks.
She greeted every caller by name when they logged on, even the ones who only came back to complain about the busy signal.
Nora remembers that she joined in on every message thread, usually at two in the morning.
Sam remembers that she never posted in a message thread, because the sysop was supposed to stay out of it.
She typed with two fingers, and she could hear the modem answer from the kitchen before anyone else did.
When the phone company changed the line in 1997, she printed the whole message archive on continuous paper and kept it in a box.
